title: Returns and Refunds Policy — 2025 (Superseded)
content:
ShopSphere Returns and Refunds Policy — 2025
Document ID: KB-001 | Version: 1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 | Status: superseded

Purpose and scope
This archived policy records the return rules that applied to ShopSphere orders delivered during calendar year 2025. It is retained for historical questions and audit comparisons. It must not be applied to orders delivered on or after 1 January 2026. When a customer asks for the current rule, use KB-002 instead. The order delivery date, not the date on which a customer first browses the help centre, determines which version applies.

Return eligibility in 2025
Most unused physical products could be returned within 14 calendar days after delivery. The customer had to include the original accessories, manuals and retail packaging where practical. Products showing accidental damage, liquid exposure, missing serial labels or signs of unauthorised repair could be rejected after inspection. A return request created after the 14-day period was normally ineligible unless a statutory right or a documented service exception applied. The 2025 electronics rule was stricter: headphones, speakers, chargers and other electronic accessories had a 7-calendar-day return window from delivery. This historical 7-day electronics window is not the current rule.

Items excluded from ordinary change-of-mind returns
Personalised products, opened hygiene products, downloadable software after activation, gift cards and items marked Final Sale were excluded from ordinary change-of-mind returns. A damaged, defective or incorrectly supplied item could still be reviewed under the applicable consumer-rights process. A support agent could not promise an exception merely because a product was excluded from change-of-mind returns.

Return request and inspection
Customers submitted a request from Order History or contacted support with the order ID and item. ShopSphere issued a return merchandise authorisation (RMA) after eligibility checks. The parcel was inspected after it reached the returns centre. The inspection outcome could be accepted, partially accepted or rejected, with a reason recorded against the RMA. A customer could ask for an explanation of the inspection decision.

Refunds under the archived policy
For an accepted return, the refund was initiated after inspection. The refund destination normally followed the original payment method, subject to payment-network limitations. The old policy did not guarantee that a bank or card issuer would post the credit on the same day.

title: Returns and Refunds Policy — 2026 (Current)
content:
ShopSphere Returns and Refunds Policy — 2026
Document ID: KB-002 | Version: 2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Purpose and version rule
This is the current ShopSphere returns policy for orders delivered on or after 1 January 2026. It supersedes KB-001 for those orders. The delivery date determines the applicable policy version. A customer who asks about a current order should receive the rules in this document, not the archived 2025 rules. If the delivery date is unknown, retrieve the order before calculating the eligibility window.

Standard return windows
Most eligible, non-personalised products may be returned within 30 calendar days from the recorded delivery date. Electronics and electronic accessories, including headphones, wireless earbuds, speakers, chargers and smart-home accessories, may be returned within 14 calendar days from delivery. The electronics rule is identified internally as RET-E14. The general rule is identified as RET-30. The final day is included until 23:59 in the delivery destination's local time. A request created within the window remains eligible for inspection even if the physical pickup occurs a few days later, provided the pickup is booked within seven calendar days of authorisation.

Condition and packaging
For a change-of-mind return, the item should be unused, complete and in resaleable condition, with included accessories and manuals. Original retail packaging is preferred but is not required where safe transport packaging is available. A product that is defective, damaged in transit or materially different from its listing is assessed under the fault or seller-error path. Do not classify a reported defect as a simple change-of-mind return without asking a short diagnostic question.

Excluded products and exceptions
Personalised goods, activated digital licences, gift cards, opened hygiene products and products labelled Final Sale are not eligible for ordinary change-of-mind returns. This exclusion does not remove a customer's right to report a fault, transit damage or an incorrect shipment. Such cases need evidence and an inspection decision. Only the designated returns supervisor can approve a policy exception; the assistant must not invent one.

Authorisation and pickup
A return request must identify the order and item, and capture a reason. The assistant checks delivery date, item eligibility and order status before offering a pickup. A return authorisation is not a completed return. The item must be handed to the carrier and inspected.

Authorisation and pickup
A return request must identify the order and item, and capture a reason. The assistant checks delivery date, item eligibility and order status before offering a pickup. A return authorisation is not a completed return. The item must be handed to the carrier and inspected. A pickup can be booked for an available date within seven calendar days after authorisation. The pickup confirmation must show the item, pickup address, date and time window. A database write to create the pickup must happen only after the customer explicitly confirms the complete summary.

Refund handling
For an accepted return, the refund is initiated after inspection. The refund method follows the original payment method unless a payment-network restriction requires an approved alternative. The refund initiation time and bank posting time are different events. See KB-003 for method-specific estimates. The assistant must distinguish “refund initiated” from “money visible in the account.”

Customer communication
Explain the applicable window, the condition requirement and the next step. If the required order or item information is missing, ask for it rather than making an eligibility promise. When the system cannot verify a rule, say that support review is required and do not fabricate a deadline.

title: Refund Processing and Payment Timelines
content:
ShopSphere Refund Processing Guide
Document ID: KB-003 | Version: 1.3 | Effective: 2026-02-01 | Status: active

Refund lifecycle
A refund has several distinct stages: return requested, return authorised, item collected, item received, inspection completed, refund initiated and payment provider posting. A customer may see the return marked accepted before the credit is visible in the bank account. Support must communicate the current stage exactly and must not describe an initiated refund as a settled bank credit. Each transition is timestamped in the order service.

Indicative processing estimates
After an accepted inspection, ShopSphere normally initiates a card refund within 2 business days. A UPI refund is normally initiated within 1 business day. A net-banking refund is normally initiated within 3 business days. A ShopSphere wallet refund is normally initiated within 4 business hours. These are initiation estimates, not guarantees for the customer's bank. The bank, card issuer or payment network may require additional time to post the credit. Weekends and bank holidays are not business days for the card and net-banking estimates.

Refund identifiers
A refund event receives a reference such as RFND-2026-10482. The payment service also records the original payment transaction reference and the masked destination. Support may share the refund reference and initiation date, but must never disclose full card numbers, UPI PINs, passwords or authentication codes. If a customer asks for a UPI PIN or OTP to “verify” a refund, explain that ShopSphere will never request it.

Partial refunds
If only one item in a multi-item order is accepted, the refund is calculated for that item and any item-specific discount allocation. Shipping charges are not automatically refunded when a customer returns one item because of change of mind. If the return is caused by a confirmed ShopSphere fulfilment error, the shipping charge may also be credited after review. The final amount is calculated by the refund service; the assistant should read that amount rather than calculate a promise from the list price.

Delayed credits
If the stated initiation estimate has passed, first check the refund event and its status. If no refund event exists, route the case to returns operations. If the event is initiated but the credit is not visible, provide the reference and suggest that the customer check with the payment provider. Escalate to Payments Support when the provider trace is older than five business days for UPI or ten business days for

title: Refund Processing and Payment Timelines
content:
initiation estimate has passed, first check the refund event and its status. If no refund event exists, route the case to returns operations. If the event is initiated but the credit is not visible, provide the reference and suggest that the customer check with the payment provider. Escalate to Payments Support when the provider trace is older than five business days for UPI or ten business days for card or net banking. Never create a second refund merely because a customer cannot yet see the first credit.

Status language
Use “initiated” when ShopSphere has sent the refund instruction, “processing” when the provider acknowledges it, and “posted” only when the provider confirms the credit. When provider status is unavailable, disclose that limitation and provide the last verified timestamp.

title: Product Exchange Policy
content:
ShopSphere Product Exchange Policy
Document ID: KB-004 | Version: 1.1 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Exchange options
An exchange replaces an eligible item with another item or variant rather than returning the purchase amount. Exchanges are subject to the same delivery-date eligibility windows as returns: 30 days for most eligible products and 14 days for electronics. The exchange service checks stock in the destination fulfilment region before presenting a replacement option. A replacement is not reserved until the customer confirms the exchange summary and the exchange record is created.

Eligible exchange reasons
Customers may request an exchange for a size or colour change, a wrong variant, or a verified product fault. A fault-related exchange may require diagnostic questions and inspection. If the requested replacement has a higher price, the customer must pay the displayed difference before confirmation. If the replacement is lower priced, the difference is handled through the refund process described in KB-003. The assistant must not invent an available replacement or a price difference; it must read current catalogue and stock results.

Exchange versus refund
A customer may choose an eligible refund instead of an exchange. The assistant should explain both paths neutrally when asked, then ask which option the customer prefers. Once an exchange is created, the same item cannot simultaneously have an open refund request. If a customer changes their mind, the current exchange state must be checked before cancelling or replacing it.

Process and confirmation
The exchange flow requires an order ID, item ID, reason, replacement selection and delivery address confirmation. The dialogue manager must collect missing slots and summarise the chosen replacement, any price difference and the expected dispatch window. The write operation is executed only after an explicit confirmation such as “Yes, place the exchange.” A vague response such as “sounds good” is not sufficient if the summary is not visible in the immediately preceding turn.

Stock and failed exchange
If the replacement is out of stock, offer a waitlist or refund option only when those options are returned by the order service. A failed stock check must not be converted into a successful exchange. Record a failure code and explain the next available action. If stock changes after the quote, revalidate it immediately before the database write.

Customer expectations
An exchange may create a new shipment and a reverse pickup. The customer should receive separate references for the return leg and replacement shipment. Do not promise that the replacement arrives on the same day as the original pickup unless the logistics service explicitly

title: Shipping, Delivery and Delivery Windows
content:
ShopSphere Shipping and Delivery Policy
Document ID: KB-005 | Version: 2.2 | Effective: 2026-03-01 | Status: active

Delivery services
ShopSphere offers Standard, Express and Scheduled delivery in supported postal codes. Standard delivery normally takes 3 to 6 business days after dispatch. Express delivery normally takes 1 to 2 business days after dispatch. Scheduled delivery provides a customer-selected window from the available slots returned by the delivery service. The estimate shown at checkout is a forecast and can change if a carrier reports a disruption. The order detail page remains the source of truth for the current shipment status.

Delivery windows and preferences
A customer may save a preferred delivery window, but a preference does not guarantee that every carrier route can honour it. Available delivery slots must be checked for the specific postal code and shipment. If a window is unavailable, offer the nearest available slot or ask the customer to select another day. The account preference is a default for future orders and can be updated or deleted on request. The assistant must distinguish a stored preference from a confirmed slot for a particular shipment.

Delivery instructions
Customers may add a short delivery instruction, such as calling on arrival or leaving a parcel with a named reception desk, where the building and carrier permit it. Instructions must not ask a carrier to leave a parcel in an unsafe, publicly accessible or weather-exposed location. A customer can ask for a saved delivery note to be changed or forgotten. Once a note is deleted from the profile store, it must not be repeated from conversation memory. The assistant should not infer a new delivery note from an old one.

Delivery exceptions
A carrier scan of “attempted” means a delivery attempt was recorded; it does not prove that the customer was contacted. “Address issue” means the carrier could not validate the address or access instructions. “Held at depot” means the parcel is awaiting a carrier action or customer instruction. For a missed attempt, the customer may use the reschedule options shown in the order service. The assistant must not promise a second attempt without checking the tracking record.

Late or lost shipments
If the estimated delivery date has passed, retrieve the latest carrier scan and compare it with the promised window. A delay of one business day can be monitored. A parcel with no scan movement for 48 hours should be referred to the carrier desk. A parcel with no movement for five calendar days may qualify for a lost-shipment investigation. Do not mark an order lost solely because

A parcel with no scan movement for 48 hours should be referred to the carrier desk. A parcel with no movement for five calendar days may qualify for a lost-shipment investigation. Do not mark an order lost solely because the customer says it has not arrived.

Fees and restrictions
Shipping fees are calculated at checkout based on service, basket and postal code. Free-shipping eligibility may depend on membership or promotion terms. Remote-area restrictions and product handling requirements can remove Express or Scheduled options. Only quote a fee returned by checkout for the actual order; examples in help content are not customer-specific prices.

title: Order and Shipment Status Codes
content:
ShopSphere Order and Shipment Status Codes
Document ID: KB-006 | Version: 1.4 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

How to read a status
An order can have an order-level status and a shipment-level status. The order-level status describes the commercial transaction; the shipment-level status describes carrier movement. A customer-facing response should use the plain-language description and include the code only when it helps the customer or support agent. Do not infer that a parcel is physically moving from an order-level status alone.

Order status codes
ORD-NEW means the order was accepted but payment or fraud checks may still be pending. ORD-PROC means payment is confirmed and the fulfilment centre is preparing the items. ORD-HOLD means fulfilment has been paused for an address, payment or inventory check. ORD-PICK means items have been picked and are undergoing packing verification. ORD-SHIP means the parcel has been handed to the carrier. ORD-DEL means the carrier has recorded delivery. ORD-CANC means the order was cancelled before dispatch. ORD-RET means a return record exists; it does not necessarily mean the refund is complete.

Shipment scan codes
SHP-LBL means a shipping label was created but the carrier has not yet scanned the parcel. SHP-PICK means the carrier collected the parcel. SHP-TRANS means the parcel is moving between carrier facilities. SHP-OUT means the parcel is out for delivery. SHP-ATT means a delivery attempt was recorded. SHP-DEP means the parcel is held at a local depot. SHP-DLV means the carrier recorded successful delivery. SHP-EXC means an exception needs investigation.

Status conflicts
If the order service says ORD-SHIP while the carrier says SHP-ATT, explain that the order was dispatched and a delivery attempt was recorded. If the order service says ORD-DEL but the customer disputes receipt, open a proof-of-delivery investigation rather than changing the status manually. When two systems disagree, report the timestamps and route the conflict to operations.

What the assistant may do
The assistant may read status and explain the code. It may not manually change a carrier scan or mark an order delivered. Status updates must come from the authorised order or carrier integration. A stale cached status should be refreshed before making a promise about delivery timing.

title: Return Authorisation and Error Codes
content:
ShopSphere Return Authorisation and Error Codes
Document ID: KB-007 | Version: 1.2 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Return identifiers
A return request receives an RMA identifier after the order, item, return window and reason pass validation. RMA-OPEN means the request is created but pickup is not yet booked. RMA-BOOK means a pickup slot is confirmed. RMA-COL means the carrier collected the item. RMA-REC means the returns centre received the parcel. RMA-INS means inspection is in progress. RMA-ACC means the return was accepted. RMA-REJ means the return was rejected after inspection. RMA-RFD means the refund instruction was initiated. These states are sequential but an item can pause between states while an external service responds.

Error codes
ERR-RMA-01 means the order identifier cannot be found. Ask the customer to verify the order ID; do not guess a similar order. ERR-RMA-02 means the requested SKU is not part of the order. Read the order items and ask the customer to select one of the listed items. ERR-RMA-03 means the item is outside the applicable return window. Explain the policy version and delivery date used. ERR-RMA-04 means a return reason is missing or invalid. Ask a concise question and do not create an RMA until a supported reason is selected. ERR-RMA-05 means the pickup slot is unavailable. Offer only slots returned by the scheduling service. ERR-RMA-06 means a confirmation token or explicit customer confirmation is missing. Do not retry the write until confirmation has been obtained.

Authorisation checks
The return service validates order ownership, delivery status, item quantity, return window and any existing open return. If an item already has an open RMA, the assistant should retrieve that RMA rather than creating a duplicate. A write timeout does not prove that the write failed; read the order return history before retrying. This prevents duplicate pickups.

Failure handling
The assistant should explain errors in plain language and state the next action. Internal stack traces, authentication tokens and payment credentials must never be shown. A support case can be created for unresolved exceptions, but the assistant must not represent a pending case as a completed return. For ERR-RMA-06, the user must see the item, reason, pickup date and time window before the final confirmation request.

Audit fields

title: Payment Methods and Payment Reference Codes
section: Payment Methods and Payment Reference Codes
content:
ShopSphere Payment Methods and Reference Codes
Document ID: KB-008 | Version: 1.5 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Supported payment methods
ShopSphere checkout may offer UPI, credit or debit card, net banking, cash on delivery in supported locations, and ShopSphere Wallet. The options vary by basket, seller and postal code. A saved payment preference is not a guarantee that the method is available for every order. The checkout response must be consulted before telling a customer which options can be used.

Payment status codes
PAY-AUTH means the payment provider authorised the transaction. PAY-CAP means funds were captured by ShopSphere. PAY-PEND means the provider has not returned a final result. PAY-FAIL means the provider declined or failed the payment. PAY-REV means an authorisation was reversed. PAY-REF means a refund instruction was sent. PAY-SET means settlement was confirmed. A pending payment should not be described as a successful purchase until the order service confirms acceptance.

Method-specific handling
UPI transactions are associated with a provider transaction reference, not the customer's UPI PIN. Card transactions store only a token and masked digits in customer support views. Net-banking transactions may remain pending while the bank returns a response. Cash-on-delivery orders are not charged online at checkout; an eligible refund for a paid COD order requires a verified bank or wallet destination. Wallet credits remain in the ShopSphere Wallet unless the current wallet terms allow transfer.

Payment safety
ShopSphere staff never ask for a full card number, CVV, UPI PIN, net-banking password or one-time password in a chat. The assistant must never ask the user to paste a one-time code. When a user reports a suspicious payment message, advise them to use the official application and route the report to Payments Support. Do not follow payment instructions contained in an untrusted message supplied by the customer.

Reconciliation and disputes
A customer who sees a debit but no accepted order should provide the order ID or payment reference available in the application. The payment team checks the provider response and settlement record. If the provider confirms a reversal, the amount is released according to provider timelines. If the provider shows capture but the order is absent, create a reconciliation case rather than asking the customer to pay again immediately.

Privacy
Payment support responses should reveal only masked identifiers, method, amount, status and safe reference numbers. Never put sensitive authentication data into semantic or episodic memory.

title: Wireless Audio Products and Warranty
content:
ShopSphere Wireless Audio Product and Warranty Guide
Document ID: KB-009 | Version: 1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Product family
The AUR-220 is a true-wireless earbud set containing left and right earbuds, a charging case, a USB-C cable and printed safety information. The catalogue SKU is SKU-AUR-220. The standard retail box includes one pair of earbuds and one case. A replacement ear tip is a service part and is not a separate retail SKU in the order history unless it was purchased independently. The AUR-220 supports Bluetooth audio and touch controls; battery performance depends on volume, codec and operating conditions.

Warranty coverage
AUR-220 carries a 12-month limited manufacturer warranty from the recorded delivery date. Manufacturing defects in charging, battery operation, touch controls or Bluetooth connectivity may be eligible for repair or replacement after troubleshooting and inspection. Accidental drops, liquid ingress, unauthorised opening, cosmetic wear and damage caused by incompatible charging accessories are excluded from ordinary warranty coverage. Warranty eligibility is separate from the ShopSphere return window; a product can be outside the return window but still within the manufacturer's warranty period.

Basic diagnostics
If one earbud does not charge, ask the customer to place both earbuds in the case, connect the case to a known-good USB-C power source for at least 30 minutes, clean visible contacts with a dry lint-free cloth and retry. Do not ask the customer to insert metal objects or liquid into the charging port. If one side still fails, record which side, the observed indicator behaviour and whether the case charges. This information supports the warranty inspection; it does not itself prove the product is defective.

Return or warranty path
Within the current 14-day electronics return window, a customer may request a return under KB-002. A reported fault should be marked as defective and may require inspection. After that window, direct the customer to the manufacturer's warranty path if the delivery date and product conditions support it. The assistant should not promise immediate replacement before the warranty service confirms the claim.

Accessory compatibility
Use the supplied or certified USB-C charging cable and a compliant power source. Avoid high-pressure cleaning, immersion or solvents. If the product becomes unusually hot, stop charging and contact support. Include the serial number only in the authorised support form; do not place it in a

title: Damaged, Incorrect or Missing Items
content:
ShopSphere Damaged, Incorrect and Missing Item Procedure
Document ID: KB-010 | Version: 1.2 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Report window and evidence
Customers should report visible transit damage, an incorrect item or a missing item as soon as possible, preferably within 48 hours of delivery. This recommended reporting period helps preserve carrier evidence; it is not a statement that statutory rights disappear after 48 hours. Ask for the order ID, affected item and a short description. Photos of the outer packaging, shipping label and affected product can help the investigation. Do not ask for unnecessary personal documents.

Damaged item
For a crushed, wet or visibly broken parcel, record the condition of the outer box and the item. If the product could be unsafe, advise the customer not to use or charge it. Create a damage case only after checking the order and item. The returns team decides whether to arrange a replacement, refund or inspection. The assistant should not promise a particular remedy before the case is reviewed.

Incorrect item
If the item delivered does not match the order line, compare the SKU and description in the order service with the product received. A wrong-item case should preserve both the ordered SKU and the reported received item. The customer should keep the packaging until the carrier or returns team provides instructions. Never tell the customer to send an unrelated item without a valid return authorisation.

Missing item in a multi-item order
A shipment may contain multiple parcels. First check whether the order has more than one shipment and whether the missing line is still in fulfilment. If all parcels are marked delivered, open a missing-item investigation. The assistant should not assume theft or accuse the carrier. The case records packing scan, parcel count, carrier proof and customer statement.

Remedy and communication
The available remedy depends on stock, fault assessment and order status. A replacement can be offered only when inventory and service eligibility are confirmed. A refund is initiated according to KB-003 after the case outcome is accepted. The response should explain what evidence is needed, what the next review step is and when the customer can expect an update. Avoid guarantees that are not present in the case system.

Escalation
A safety-related defect, repeated packing error or high-value missing item should be escalated to the relevant operations queue. If the issue involves potential account compromise or payment fraud, use the security route rather than the ordinary returns queue.

title: Order Cancellation Policy
content:
ShopSphere Order Cancellation Policy
Document ID: KB-011 | Version: 1.1 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

When an order can be cancelled
An order can normally be cancelled while it is in ORD-NEW or ORD-PROC, provided the fulfilment centre has not begun a restricted packing or dispatch step. Once the order is handed to the carrier and reaches ORD-SHIP, the standard cancellation action is unavailable; the customer may need to use the return process after delivery. The order service is the authority on whether cancellation is still possible. The assistant must not infer cancellation eligibility from an estimated delivery date.

Cancellation request flow
Collect the order ID and reason. Read the order state and check for existing cancellation requests. If cancellation is available, show the order items and the cancellation consequence, including any payment reversal estimate returned by the payment service. Ask the customer to confirm the cancellation. Only after an explicit confirmation should the assistant invoke the cancellation write. A request such as “Can I cancel?” is a question, not authorisation to cancel.

Partial cancellation
Some orders contain several items or shipments. Partial cancellation is allowed only when the order service exposes an item-level cancellation action. If one item has already shipped, the assistant must not claim the whole order is cancelled. It should explain which lines can still be cancelled and ask the customer how to proceed. Discounts and shipping charges may be recalculated when an item is removed.

Payment reversal
If payment was authorised but not captured, cancellation may result in an authorisation reversal rather than a refund. If payment was captured, the payment service initiates a refund under the applicable method timeline in KB-003. The two events should not be described as identical. A pending provider response should be communicated as pending.

Failure and recovery
If the cancellation service returns a timeout, retrieve the order again before retrying. A timeout may occur after the write has succeeded. Duplicate cancellation attempts can create confusing audit records, so read-after-write verification is required. If the order is no longer cancellable, explain the next legitimate option instead of attempting a bypass.

title: ShopSphere Membership Benefits
content:
ShopSphere Membership Benefits Guide
Document ID: KB-012 | Version: 1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Membership tiers
ShopSphere currently offers Basic, Plus and Gold membership tiers. The tier displayed in the customer profile is authoritative; a customer statement alone does not change the account tier. Basic members receive standard order tracking and access to ordinary support channels. Plus members may receive selected shipping promotions and priority support for eligible orders. Gold members may receive free standard shipping on eligible baskets, priority chat routing and an extended service window for selected product categories where the promotion terms explicitly say so.

Benefits are conditional
Membership benefits vary by category, seller, basket amount and postal code. A free-shipping benefit is not guaranteed on bulky goods, remote-area deliveries or marketplace items excluded by the offer. Priority support is a queueing benefit, not a promise of immediate resolution. An assistant should read the benefit eligibility for the actual customer and order before claiming a discount or service level.

Profile facts and preferences
A customer's communication preference, saved delivery window and delivery note are profile data separate from membership tier. A customer can request an update or deletion of these preferences. Do not infer a communication channel from the last message alone; use the current saved preference unless the customer updates it. A forget request must remove the targeted profile fact and any memory references that would reproduce it later.

Promotions
Membership promotions may have start and end dates. A promotion that has expired must not be described as currently available. When multiple offers apply, the checkout service determines the final combination. The assistant may explain published terms but should not calculate an unverified final price.

Privacy and account access
The assistant may use membership information only after the customer is authenticated in the application context. Do not reveal another customer's tier, address or order information. If identity or ownership is uncertain, ask the customer to sign in through the official application and do not bypass the account access check.

title: Reverse Pickup Scheduling and Packaging Guide
section: Reverse Pickup Scheduling and Packaging Guide
content:
ShopSphere Reverse Pickup and Packaging Guide
Document ID: KB-013 | Version: 1.3 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Pickup eligibility
A reverse pickup can be scheduled after a return or exchange is authorised. The selected date must be available in the pickup service and, under the current standard flow, must fall within seven calendar days after authorisation. The return request must identify the correct order and item. A pickup booking is not proof that the carrier collected the parcel. The carrier scan is required to move the return to the collected state.

Scheduling windows
Pickup services may offer morning, afternoon and evening windows depending on the postal code and carrier capacity. An evening slot is not guaranteed merely because the customer has a saved delivery preference. The scheduler must return an available slot for the actual return address. If a requested slot is full, show the nearest alternatives and ask the customer to choose. Never silently substitute a different date or time window.

Customer confirmation
Before creating a pickup, show the order ID, item description, return reason, pickup date, time window and address summary. The customer must confirm that summary. The write operation should include the confirmation source and timestamp. If the customer changes a date or time after confirming, present a new summary and obtain confirmation again. “Proceed” may count as confirmation only when the immediately preceding assistant message clearly showed the complete action summary.

Packaging
Use a strong outer carton or approved return pouch. Protect fragile items with sufficient cushioning and prevent loose accessories from moving inside the package. Include only the items listed in the return authorisation. Remove or cover old shipping labels so the carrier scans the correct return label. Do not include batteries or hazardous materials unless the carrier instructions explicitly permit them.

Missed pickup
If the carrier misses the scheduled pickup, first check the carrier event. If no attempt was recorded, create a reschedule request using the next available slot. If the carrier records an unsuccessful attempt, explain the scan and ask whether the customer wants another available slot. Do not create a second RMA for the same item. Keep the existing RMA identifier and add a pickup reschedule event.

Handover evidence
At collection, the carrier should scan the return label and provide a pickup receipt or digital confirmation. The customer should retain the receipt until the return is accepted or the refund is initiated. If the carrier takes the parcel without a scan, escalate with the pickup reference and timestamp.

title: Customer Support Service Levels and Escalation
section: Customer Support Service Levels and Escalation
content:
ShopSphere Customer Support Service Levels and Escalation
Document ID: KB-014 | Version: 1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Support channels
Customers can contact ShopSphere through in-app chat, email and the help centre. Channel availability may vary by time and account tier. A saved preference indicates how the customer would like routine updates; it does not prevent the customer from choosing a different channel during an active interaction. Sensitive account changes must be completed in the authenticated application rather than by replying to an unverified email.

Routine service targets
The standard target for a routine email response is within two business days. In-app chat is queued according to current staffing and does not guarantee an immediate human response. A return inspection update is normally provided within three business days after receipt at the returns centre. These are service targets, not guarantees that every case will be resolved within that time. The assistant should check the case timestamp before stating that a target has been missed.

Escalation categories
Use RETURNS-OPS for RMA, inspection and pickup exceptions; PAYMENTS for refund or settlement mismatches; CARRIER-DESK for parcel movement and missed delivery; CATALOGUE for inaccurate product listings; and ACCOUNT-SECURITY for suspected account takeover or fraudulent payment requests. A case should include the order ID, relevant event reference, a concise issue summary and evidence already supplied. Do not copy passwords, OTPs or full payment credentials into a case.

Priority handling
Safety concerns, suspected fraud, repeated failed delivery attempts and high-value missing items require expedited triage. Membership priority may affect queue order where the account benefits say so, but it does not override security or safety procedures. The assistant must not mark a case as resolved until the owning team records an outcome.

Updates and ownership
A support case has an owner queue, status, created timestamp and next-update target. If an escalation is created, provide the case reference and explain which team owns the next action. If the system cannot create a case, disclose that it could not be completed and provide the approved contact route. Do not claim that an escalation has been submitted without a returned case ID.

title: Gift Cards, Discount Codes and Promotion Rules
section: Gift Cards, Discount Codes and Promotion Rules
content:
ShopSphere Gift Cards and Promotion Rules
Document ID: KB-015 | Version: 1.2 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Status: active

Gift cards
A ShopSphere gift card is a prepaid stored-value instrument that can be redeemed at checkout for eligible products. The gift card code should be entered only in the official ShopSphere checkout. Support agents must never ask a customer to share a complete unused gift card code in a public chat. A partially masked reference is sufficient for most investigations. Gift cards are not eligible for ordinary change-of-mind returns once delivered, although a proven activation or balance error can be investigated.

Discount codes
A promotion code may be restricted by start date, expiry date, product category, seller, minimum basket amount or membership tier. A code that is expired or excluded by the promotion terms should not be promised as valid. The checkout service calculates the final discount and is authoritative when multiple offers are present. The assistant may explain why a code failed when the response includes a reason, but must not invent an alternative code.

Stacking and refunds
Unless the offer explicitly permits stacking, only one promotional code can be applied to a basket. When a discounted item is returned, the refund service calculates the item-level amount after allocating the discount. The customer should receive the amount returned by the refund service, not a manual calculation based on the undiscounted catalogue price. Shipping promotions may be reversed if the remaining basket no longer meets the offer conditions.

Examples of internal references
PROMO-GOLD-SHIP is an illustrative identifier for the Gold standard-shipping promotion. GFT-ACT-01 identifies a gift-card activation investigation. DISC-EXP-02 identifies an expired promotion code response. These references help support teams classify an issue; they are not customer redemption codes. A customer-facing response should not imply that an internal reference can be entered at checkout.

Fraud prevention
If a customer reports a message asking them to buy gift cards and send photographs or codes, treat it as a potential scam. Advise them not to share the code and route the report to ACCOUNT-SECURITY. ShopSphere will not request gift card codes to release a parcel, approve a refund or verify an account.

title: Shipping and Delivery Policy — 2025 (Superseded)
content:
ShopSphere Shipping and Delivery Policy — 2025
Document ID: KB-016 | Version: 1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 | Status: superseded

Purpose and applicability
This archived shipping policy applied to orders placed from 1 January through 31 December 2025. It is retained to explain historical delivery estimates and must not be used to quote current service levels for orders placed on or after 1 January 2026. For a current order, use KB-005, version 2.2. Check the order creation date and the service displayed at checkout before deciding which policy applies. A customer's saved delivery preference is not itself a carrier booking.

Historical delivery estimates
Under the 2025 Standard service, delivery normally took 4 to 7 business days after dispatch. Express delivery normally took 2 to 3 business days after dispatch in supported postal codes. These were estimates rather than guaranteed arrival dates. The actual carrier scan history remained the source of truth once a parcel left the fulfilment centre. Scheduled delivery was available only in selected service areas and only when the checkout service returned a slot.

Delivery attempts and exceptions
A carrier attempt could be recorded even when the customer did not receive a call or message. Customers were asked to check the shipment page for a reschedule option. An address validation issue, depot hold or weather disruption could change the estimated arrival date. Support staff had to read the latest carrier scan before explaining a delay and could not manually mark a shipment as delivered.

Delivery instructions
Customers could add a short instruction, such as a safe reception handover, subject to the carrier's building-access rules. The carrier could reject instructions that asked for a parcel to be left in an exposed or publicly accessible place. Customers could request that a saved note be updated or removed from their profile. Removal from the profile did not authorise staff to repeat the note in later conversations.

Fees and service restrictions
Shipping fees were calculated at checkout using the service, basket, product handling requirements and postal code. Remote areas and bulky products could be excluded from Express service. Promotional free shipping was subject to the offer terms and did not automatically apply to every seller or product. Support could explain published rules but had to rely on the checkout result for a customer-specific fee.

Version comparison
The current 2026 schedule is faster for some routes
